evidence.title: The Dark Tower (series)
evidence.text: The Dark Tower is a series of eight books written by American author Stephen King that incorporates themes from multiple genres, including dark fantasy, science fantasy, horror, and Western.

evidence.title: The Dark Tower (series)
evidence.text: It describes a "gunslinger" and his quest toward a tower, the nature of which is both physical and metaphorical.

evidence.title: The Dark Tower (series)
evidence.text: The series, and its use of the Dark Tower, expands upon Stephen King's multiverse and in doing so, links together many of his other novels.

evidence.title: The Dark Tower (series)
evidence.text: King has described the series as his "magnum opus".

evidence.title: The Dark Tower (series)
evidence.text: In addition to the eight novels of the series proper that comprise 4,250 pages, many of King's other books relate to the story, introducing concepts and characters that come into play as the series progresses.

evidence.title: Dark Tower (game)
evidence.text: Dark Tower is a 1981 electronic board game by Milton Bradley Company, for one to four players.

evidence.title: Dark Tower (game)
evidence.text: The object of the game is to amass an army, collect the three keys to the Tower, and defeat the evil within.

evidence.title: Dark Tower (game)
evidence.text: The game came out during the height of the role-playing game craze in the early 1980s.

evidence.title: Dark Tower (game)
evidence.text: Advertising for the game included a television commercial featuring Orson Welles.

evidence.title: Almoayyed Tower
evidence.text: Almoayyed Tower (also known as: Dark Tower), is commercial skyscraper located in the Seef neighborhood of Bahraini capital Manama.

evidence.title: Almoayyed Tower
evidence.text: The tower is regular four-sided structure, with a height of 172 m .

evidence.title: Almoayyed Tower
evidence.text: Almoayyed consists mostly of office and business complexes.

evidence.title: Almoayyed Tower
evidence.text: It was a tallest tower in Bahrain until the Bahrain Financial Harbour, Bahrain WTC and the Abraj Al Lulu was constructed.

evidence.title: Almoayyed Tower
evidence.text: Almoayyed Tower is also known as "Dark Tower" because of its dark coloring.

evidence.title: Almoayyed Tower
evidence.text: Almoayyed Tower is currently managed by Cluttons.

evidence.title: Downfall (game)
evidence.text: Downfall is a two-player game for players aged 7 and older, first marketed by the Milton Bradley Company in 1970.

evidence.title: Crimson King
evidence.text: The Crimson King, known to some as Los' or Ram Abbalah, is a fictional character created by Stephen King.

evidence.title: Crimson King
evidence.text: He is the primary antagonist of King's eight-volume "Dark Tower" series, as well as the novels "Insomnia" and "Black House".

evidence.title: Crimson King
evidence.text: Described as "Gan's crazy side", the Crimson King is the ultimate ruler of the Red (also called the Random and the Outer Dark), and the archetypal embodiment of evil in Stephen King's fictional multiverse.

evidence.title: Crimson King
evidence.text: His goal is to topple the Dark Tower which serves as the linchpin of time and space, destroying the multitude of universes which revolve around it so that he can rule in the primordial chaos which follows.

evidence.title: Robin Furth
evidence.text: Robin Furth was the personal research assistant to Stephen King and the author of Stephen King's "The Dark Tower: A Complete Concordance", which was published by Scribner on December 5, 2006.

evidence.title: Robin Furth
evidence.text: It is a compilation of her two previous encyclopedic books dealing with King's magnum opus, "The Dark Tower: A Concordance, volume I" - which explores the first four books in King's series - and "A Concordance II", which gives the reader definitions and explanations of pivotal terms used over the course of the final three books of The Dark Tower.

evidence.title: Robin Furth
evidence.text: She is now currently working on the graphic novel adaptation of the Dark Tower for Marvel Comics .

evidence.title: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole
evidence.text: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole (also known as Dark Tower 4.5) is a fantasy novel by American writer Stephen King, first published on February 21, 2012 by Grant as a limited edition, and later published by Scribner as a trade hardcover (ISBN  ) on April 24, 2012, with ebook and audiobook editions.

evidence.text: The audiobook is read by the author.

evidence.title: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole
evidence.text: As part of "The Dark Tower" series, it is the eighth novel, but chronologically set between volumes and .
evidence.resolved_title: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole

evidence.title: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole
evidence.text: First mentioned by King in 2009, after the series had been proclaimed as concluded in 2004 with the publication of the , it was announced on the author's official site on March 10, 2011.
evidence.resolved_title: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole

evidence.title: The Dark Tower: The Wind Through the Keyhole
evidence.text: A short excerpt was released online on December 19, 2011, the day the limited edition of the novel became available for pre-order.

evidence.title: All-World
evidence.text: All-World is a fictional location in Stephen King's "The Dark Tower" series of novels.

evidence.title: All-World
evidence.text: All-World is the world known to contain the "Keystone Tower" in the Dark Tower series.

evidence.title: All-World
evidence.text: It is the only world that contains the Dark Tower in its physical form; all others contain a representative of the Tower, such as a rose.

evidence.title: All-World
evidence.text: From All-World, it is possible to actually enter the Dark Tower.
